856: ## 7. Layer 7 — Plugin Installation & Backend Selection Protocol
857: 
858: Mise plugins frequently exist under multiple competing backends
859: (`asdf:`, `vfox:`, `github:`, `aqua:`, `ubi:`). The choice is **not
860: interchangeable** — different backends ship different binaries, manage
861: their own install roots, and have different SSH / HTTPS reachability
862: profiles on different networks. This Layer runs **before** Layers 1–6:
863: no version pin, no trust prompt, no `mise install` invocation can
864: succeed if the underlying plugin is missing or installed under a
865: backend that doesn't resolve in the current environment.
866: 
867: ### 7.1 Detection
868: 
869: Apply this Layer whenever:
870: 
871: - The user issues `mise install <plugin>` (single-plugin install)
872: - The user issues `mise install` in a project folder and it fails with
873:   a plugin-resolution error (e.g., `plugin <name> not found`, SSH
874:   authentication failure resolving an `asdf:` or `vfox:` URL, or
875:   `mise registry` returning multiple candidates)
876: - A `mise.toml` references a tool whose plugin is not yet installed
877:   locally (`mise plugins --user` does not list it)
878: 
879: ### 7.2 Backend Inventory
880: 
881: Query the mise registry for all available backends for the plugin:
882: 
883: ```bash
884: # Show every registered backend for a given tool name
885: mise registry <plugin>
886: ```
887: 
888: If the output lists more than one entry (e.g., `dart` may show
889: `asdf:asdf-community/asdf-dart` and `vfox:version-fox/vfox-dart`), the
890: plugin has **multiple backends** and the user MUST choose explicitly —
891: never auto-pick the first match.
892: 
893: ### 7.3 Presentation to User
894: 
895: Present a numbered table of every backend candidate with its full
896: GitHub URL and a brief differentiator:
897: 
898: | # | Backend | Repo | Notes |
899: |---|---|---|---|
900: | 1 | `asdf:` | `asdf-community/asdf-dart` | Mature, large user base |
901: | 2 | `vfox:` | `version-fox/vfox-dart`    | Newer, cross-platform Lua plugin runtime |
902: 
903: Ask the user which to install. Do NOT proceed without an explicit
904: choice.
905: 
906: ### 7.4 Installation — Full GitHub URL Form
907: 
908: Once the user has chosen a backend, install the plugin using the
909: **full HTTPS GitHub URL** of the chosen backend's repository:
910: 
911: ```bash
912: mise plugins install <plugin> https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git
913: ```
914: 
915: **Forbidden form — `vfox:` / `asdf:` URL prefixes:**
916: 
917: ```bash
918: # ❌ DO NOT USE — these prefixes cause SSH auth failures on networks
919: #    that lack a configured GitHub SSH key, even when the user is
920: #    fully authenticated for HTTPS clones.
921: mise plugins install <plugin> vfox:version-fox/vfox-<plugin>
922: mise plugins install <plugin> asdf:asdf-community/asdf-<plugin>
923: ```
924: 
925: The HTTPS `.git` URL form sidesteps the SSH-key requirement and works
926: identically on Gitpod, Cloud Shell, NeverInstall, plain Ubuntu, macOS,
927: and Windows.
928: 
929: ### 7.5 Triggering the Tool Install
930: 
931: **`mise.toml` precedence — Layer 7 never overrides it.** Layer 7
932: activates only when (a) the user issues a bare-plugin
933: `mise install <plugin>` outside of `mise.toml` control, or (b) a
934: project-folder `mise install` has already failed with a plugin-
935: resolution error. While `mise.toml` resolves cleanly, Layer 7 is a
936: no-op; the agent MUST NOT pre-emptively prompt for a backend choice
937: on plugins that `mise.toml` is silently happy with.
938: 
939: After the plugin lands, invoke the actual tool install. Two cases:
940:

1132: ## 9. Post-Edit File Validation Protocol
1133: 
1134: After **any** edit to a project file, the agent MUST validate the file using its
1135: industrial-standard tool before proceeding. This catches formatting errors (e.g. stray
1136: indentation) introduced by automated edits.
1137: 
1138: > The validation tools listed here are **system-wide tools**. Ensure they are installed
1139: > using the [System-Wide Tool Management Skill](../system-wide-tool-management/SKILL.md)
1140: > before running these commands.

1142: ### 9.1 Validation Commands by File Type
1143: 
1144: | File | Tool | Syntax Check | Format Check & Fix |
1145: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
1146: | `mise.toml` | `taplo` | `taplo check <absolute_path>` | `taplo fmt --check <absolute_path>` / `taplo fmt <absolute_path>` |
1147: | `requirements.txt` | `pip` | `pip install --dry-run -r <absolute_path>` | N/A (no formatter) |
1148: | `*.md` Markdown | `markdownlint-cli2` | `markdownlint-cli2 <absolute_path>` | `markdownlint-cli2 --fix <absolute_path>` |
1149: | `*.py` Python | `pylint` via `mise exec` | `mise exec --cd <project_dir> python@<ver> -- python -m pylint <absolute_path>` | Manual fix per error |
1150: 
1151: > **Note on Python Errors & Formatting:**
1152: >
1153: > - `pylint` is a strict, comprehensive linter. It highlights semantic and structural
1154: >   errors (e.g., missing docstrings, generic exceptions, complexity limits) which
1155: >   **must be fixed manually** via code edits.
1156: > - **DO NOT manually fix Pylint errors** before exhausting auto-fixers. You MUST use
1157: >   specialized formatters and auto-fixers first to resolve stylistic and structural
1158: >   complaints automatically.
1159: > - **Primary Industrial Standard**: Use **`ruff check --fix`** and **`ruff format`** first.
1160: >   It is drastically faster and can auto-fix many structural and code-style issues.
1161: > - **Secondary Standard (Fallback)**: If `ruff` cannot be used, youMUST use **`black`**.
1162: >   `black` is the definitive, uncompromising Python code formatter and was the
1163: >   industry standard before `ruff`. (Only use `autopep8` as a last-resort legacy fallback).
1164: > - Only after running these auto-fixers should you manually fix any remaining semantic
1165: >   Pylint errors (e.g., missing docstrings, complex logic).
1166: > - Because these are Python tools, they MUST follow Layer 4: add them to
1167: >   `requirements.txt` and run them via `mise exec`.

1169: ### 9.2 `mise.toml` Validation & Formatting (`taplo`)
1170: 
1171: > **Important distinction:**
1172: >
1173: > - `taplo check` — validates TOML **syntax** (parse errors, duplicate keys). A file can
1174: >   pass `check` but still be incorrectly formatted.
1175: > - `taplo fmt --check` — verifies **formatting** (indentation, spacing, alignment).
1176: > - `taplo fmt` — **auto-fixes** formatting in place; run after `check` passes.
1177:

1180: ```bash

1189: taplo fmt /absolute/path/to/project/mise.toml
1190: 
1191: # Step 4 — Re-run formatting check to confirm clean

Pushing a safety stash on top of an unclassified 84: stash stack creates ambiguity at verification time about which 85: `stash@{N}` is "ours." 86: 87: #### 1b — Author a descriptive snapshot message 88: 89: The message MUST encode at minimum: 90: 91: - Purpose token `safety:` (distinct from feature WIP, mixed work, 92: triage-bucket markers). 93: - A short description of the upcoming sequence (e.g., 94: `pre-batch-2 snapshot of commits 7..11 family-unit introduction`). 95: - A change-count summary (e.g., `12 modified + 8 untracked`). 96: - An ISO date (e.g., `2026-05-17`). 97: 98: Example: 99: 100: ```text 101: safety: pre-batch-1-remainder snapshot of 14 modified + 8 untracked entries before commits 5..N land (2026-05-17) 102: ``` 103: 104: The `safety:` prefix is the canonical marker that lets the verification 105: phase (and any future triage) identify this stash entry unambiguously. 106: 107: #### 1c — Push the snapshot with untracked files included 108: 109: ```powershell 110: git -C stash push -u -m "" 111: ``` 112: 113: The `-u` flag is MANDATORY — untracked files are first-class working-tree 114: state per the §3.3 mandate, and a snapshot without them defeats the 115: rollback purpose for any sequence that introduces new files. 116: 117: #### 1d — Immediately apply back 118: 119: ```powershell 120: git -C stash apply 121: ``` 122: 123: **Apply, NOT pop.** Pop would drop the stash entry on success, defeating 124: the rollback contract. `apply` leaves the entry intact on the stash stack 125: while restoring every line to the working tree. 126: 127: #### 1e — Verify post-apply parity 128: 129: ```powershell 130: git -C status --short | Measure-Object | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Count 131: ``` 132: 133: The line count MUST equal the pre-stash status line count. Should I try again? (y/n) 152: ... 153: warning: failed to remove : Permission denied 154: ``` 155: 156: The stash push itself succeeded (verify with 1e step 2); only the apply 157: is partial. Recovery options, in order of preference: 158: 159: 1. **Close the indexing tool window** for the affected workspace (or 160: stop the JDT Language Server / Eclipse builder), then re-run 161: `git stash apply`. The second apply typically succeeds. 162: 2. **Move the offending directory out of the way** (`Move-Item`), re-run 163: apply, then restore the moved directory by `git checkout -- ` 164: if it is tracked or by `Move-Item` back if untracked. 165: 3. **Apply via an isolated worktree** per 166: [`git-dependent-branch-restack-cascade`](../git-dependent-branch-restack-cascade/SKILL.md) 167: §4.6 pattern, then cherry-pick the apply into the main worktree. 168: 169: In all cases the stash entry MUST remain on the stack — never `pop` 170: during recovery. 171: 172: #### 1g — Stash-Apply Conflict Recovery via Selective File Extraction 173: 174: When `git stash apply` fails because a live editor (VS Code, Copilot, 175: Eclipse, IntelliJ) rewrote files between the `push` and `apply` commands, 176: the standard recovery options in 1f (close editor → retry apply, move 177: offending directory) may not work — the editor instantly regenerates the 178: conflicting files. Do NOT retry `git stash apply`; each retry reproduces 179: the same conflicts. Instead, extract files **selectively** from the intact 180: stash entry as each commit in the planned sequence is executed. 181: 182: **Prerequisite**: You MUST have an approved Arranged Commits Preview (from 183: [`git-atomic-commit-construction`](../git-atomic-commit-construction/SKILL.md) 184: §3 — the Verbose Display) that lists every planned commit and the files 185: it needs. Without this plan, selective extraction has no target. 186: 187: **Procedure — repeat for each planned commit in sequence:** 188: 189: 1. **Identify needed files**. From the Arranged Commits Preview, list the 190: exact file paths the current commit requires. 191: 192: 2. **Compare each file against the stash**. For every file the commit needs: 193: - **If tracked** (exists in HEAD): `git diff stash@{0} -- ` shows 194: whether the stash holds a different version. An empty output means the 195: working tree already matches the stash; skip extraction. 196: - **If untracked** (new file not yet in HEAD): `git ls-tree stash@{0}^3` 197: lists untracked files captured by the `-u` flag. Check if `` 198: appears in that listing. 199: 200: 3. **Extract the desired stash version**: 201: - **Tracked files**: `git checkout stash@{0} -- ` 202: - **Untracked files**: `git show stash@{0}^3: > ` 203: (The `^3` suffix addresses the untracked-tree parent of a stash — 204: `stash@{0}^3` is the tree object that `git stash push -u` captured.) 205: 206: 4. **Verify extraction**: 207: 208: ```bash 209: git diff 210: # MUST show the stashed content now present in the working tree 211: # (no diff means the working tree already matched stash) 212: ``` 213: 214: 5. **Stage and commit** per the approved plan using normal atomic-commit 215: construction procedures (`git add `, `git commit -m "..."`). 216: 217: 6. **Repeat** for the next planned commit. 218: 219: **Example** — commit 1 needs `src/foo.ts` and `src/bar.ts`: 220: 221: ```bash 222: # Compare tracked files against stash 223: git diff stash@{0} -- src/foo.ts # shows stash has changes 224: git diff stash@{0} -- src/bar.ts # empty — working tree matches 225: 226: # Extract foo.ts from stash 227: git checkout stash@{0} -- src/foo.ts 228: 229: # Verify extraction 230: git diff src/foo.ts # no diff = correct 231: 232: # Stage and commit per plan 233: git add src/foo.ts src/bar.ts 234: git commit -m "feat(foo): implement core logic" 235: ``` 236: 237: **Safety guarantees**: 238: 239: - The stash entry (`stash@{0}`) is NEVER modified by `git checkout 240: stash@{0} -- ` or `git show stash@{0}^3:` — these are 241: read-only operations against the stash object. The stash remains 242: intact for end-of-session Phase 3 verification. 243: - Files whose working-tree version was intentionally preferred over 244: the stash version (e.g., because the live editor's changes are 245: desired) are simply skipped in step 2 — no extraction, no conflict. 246: - After all planned commits land, proceed to **Phase 3** 247: (Verify-and-Release) as normal. The stash is retained for the full 248: verification cycle; it MUST NOT be dropped without user authorization 249: per Phase 3d. 250: 251: **When NOT to use this procedure**: 252: 253: - The stash apply succeeded (even partially). Use Phase 1e/1f instead. 254: - You do not have an Arranged Commits Preview identifying per-commit 255: files. Without a plan, you cannot know which files belong to which 256: commit — abort and re-plan first. 257: - The stash itself is corrupted or missing (`git stash list` shows no 258: `safety:` entry). A fresh Phase 1 capture is required. 259: - The stash is **not a safety stash** (no `safety:` prefix) — it is a 260: stale or pre-existing stash. These remain after release. 304: - **Unexpected**: Files that should be in HEAD but aren't — investigate 305: before release. The stash MUST be retained 333: for forensic recovery. Re-investigate before any drop. 334: - **Merge conflicts during 3b apply** → The working tree has diverged 335: from the snapshot in a way that would discard snapshot content. 336: Resolve manually using `git checkout -- ` from the stash, or 337: abort with `git checkout .` and investigate. The stash MUST be retained. 338: 339: #### 3c.1 — Optional: stronger per-file content audit 340: 341: The `stash apply` no-op check in 3c proves the working tree didn't *change* 342: when the stash was re-applied — strong evidence that snapshot content is in 343: HEAD, but it is a *delta*-level check. Recommend re-running 3b after any 374: further commits to re-verify. 375: - **inspect-first** → Run `git stash show -u stash@{0}` and `git stash 376: show -p stash@{0}` for full content review before deciding. 377: 378: The drop MUST NOT be automated even when 3c is clean — per 379: [`git-operation-rules.md` §5](../../../ai-agent-rules/git-operation-rules.md), 380: every destructive stash operation requires explicit per-stash user 381: authorization. 382: 383: --- 384: 385: ## Composition by Higher-Level Skills 386: 387: | Composer Skill | Role of this skill in the pipeline | 388: |---|---| 389: | [`git-atomic-commit-construction`](../git-atomic-commit-construction/SKILL.md) §3.3 | Mandatory invocation before the first commit of any sequence of ≥ 2 commits, including every batch under §3.2 Batch-by-Batch Authorization. | 390: | [`git-history-refinement`](../git-history-refinement/SKILL.md) | Captures the working tree before destructive history rewrites, providing a rollback path independent of the backup branch (which only covers committed history). | 391: | [`git-rebase-standardization`](../git-rebase-standardization/SKILL.md) | Captures the working tree before any rebase that runs against a dirty tree (the rebase will otherwise refuse or stash-implicitly). | 392: | [`git-commit-edit`](../git-commit-edit/SKILL.md) | Captures the working tree before interactive rebase with hunk-splitting. | 393: 394: ## Related Skills 395: 396: | Skill | Relationship | 397: |---|---| 398: | [`git-stash-triage`](../git-stash-triage/SKILL.md) | **Prerequisite when stash list is non-empty at Phase 1a.** Classifies pre-existing stash entries so the `safety:` push lands at a known position on the stack. 12: > **Version:** 1.0.0
13: > **Standard:** [Agent Skills (agentskills.io)](https://agentskills.io) 14: 15: ## Description 16: 17: When constructing a commit, the agent must deliver the message to `git commit` 18: without shell-escaping failures and verify the resulting commit contains the 19: expected files. This skill documents three delivery patterns with clear 20: selection criteria, plus the reliable verification technique. 21: 22: ### Message Delivery Problem 23: 24: `git commit -m '...'` breaks when the message contains: 25: 26: | Character | Why it breaks | 27: |-----------|---------------| 28: | `'` (single quote) | Closes the shell quoting — `it's` becomes `git commit -m 'it'` with trailing `s'` as garbage | 29: | `$` (dollar sign) | Triggers variable expansion — `$variable` is replaced by its value | 30: | `` ` `` (backtick) | Starts subshell execution | 31: | Newlines | Multi-line `-m` messages are fragile across shells | 32: 33: ### Verification Problem 34: 35: `git show --stat` truncates long file paths to fit terminal width: 36: 37: ``` 38: .../ai-agent-rules/git-operation-rules.md 39: ``` 40: 41: A `grep` or `Select-String` on the stat output may miss matches because the 42: truncated path no longer matches the expected string. `--name-only` outputs 43: every file path in full with no truncation. 44: 45: --- 46: 47: ## 1. Delivery Pattern Reference 48: 49: ### 1.1 `-m` (Simple single-line messages) 50: 51: Safe when the message is a single line with no `"`, `$`, or `` ` `` characters. 52: 53: ```bash 54: git commit -m "docs(rules): add widget lifecycle protocol" 55: ``` 56: 57: **Limitations:** 58: - `'` is safe inside double-quoted `-m` in bash/zsh, but `'` inside `-m '...'` breaks 59: - `$` and `` ` `` must be escaped (`\$`, `` \` ``) 60: - Newlines require fragile `\n` concatenation 61: - **Forbidden for multi-line messages or any content that contains characters whose shell interaction is uncertain** 62: 63: ### 1.2 Heredoc → `-F` (Safe for all content) 64: 65: **RECOMMENDED for multi-line or special-character messages.** Use a heredoc to 66: write the message to a temp file, then pass via `-F`: 67: 68: ```bash 69: cat > /tmp/commit_msg <<'EOF' 70: feat(api): add user registration endpoint 71: 72: - Implements POST /api/v1/users with validation 73: - Adds email uniqueness check before insert 74: - Returns 201 with user ID on success 75: EOF 76: 77: git commit -F /tmp/commit_msg 78: ``` 79: 80: **Key details:** 81: - `<<'EOF'` (quoted delimiter) prevents ALL shell interpolation — `$`, `` ` ``, and `'` are passed verbatim 82: - Use a unique temp file path per invocation: `/tmp/commit_msg.$$` or `/tmp/commit_msg.$(date +%s)` 83: - `git commit -F` reads the file; no shell parsing of the message occurs 84: - Clean up: `rm -f /tmp/commit_msg` immediately after the commit succeeds 85: 86: **Why not embed inside `-m` with `$()`?** `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ...)"` still 87: exposes the message to the shell's `-m` argument parsing; any characters that 88: interact with the outer double-quoting (`"`, `$`, `` ` ``) can still break. 89: 90: ### 1.3 `GIT_EDITOR` script (Reword / Amend) 91: 92: When Git invokes the editor for `reword`, `amend`, or interactive rebase, delegate 93: message writing to a script that replaces `$1`: 94: 95: ```bash 96: cat > /tmp/commit_msg.sh <<'SCRIPT' 97: #!/bin/sh 98: cat > "$1" <<'MSG' 99: feat(api): add user registration 100: 101: Implementation notes: 102: - Uses bcrypt for password hashing 103: - Rate-limited to 10 requests/min per IP 104: MSG 105: SCRIPT 106: 107: chmod +x /tmp/commit_msg.sh 108: GIT_EDITOR=/tmp/commit_msg.sh git commit --amend 109: rm -f /tmp/commit_msg.sh 110: ``` 111: 112: This is the canonical pattern used by 113: [`git-commit-message-reword`](../git-commit-message-reword/SKILL.md) and 114: [`git-commit-message-bulk-reword`](../git-commit-message-bulk-reword/SKILL.md). 115: 116: --- 117: 118: ## 2. Verification Pattern 119: 120: ### 2.1 Reliable file listing — `--name-only` 121: 122: After a commit, verify the file set with: 123: 124: ```bash 125: git show --name-only HEAD 126: ``` 127: 128: This outputs every file path in full, one per line. Pipe to `grep` for targeted 129: checks: 130: 131: ```bash 132: git show --name-only HEAD | grep "git-operation-rules.md" 133: ``` 134: 135: Use this for **programmatic path matching** — it never truncates. 136: 137: ### 2.2 Full diff inspection 138: 139: When you need to verify both the file set AND the content: 140: 141: ```bash 142: git show HEAD # full diff with paths 143: git show --stat HEAD # summary with line counts 144: ``` 145: 146: Use `--stat` only for human-readable summaries, never for programmatic path 147: matching. 148: 149: ### 2.3 Detecting stat truncation 150: 151: If `--stat` output is the only data available, detect truncation by checking 152: for leading `...`: 153: 154: ```bash 155: git show --stat HEAD | grep '\.\.\./' 156: ``` 157: 158: Any match indicates path truncation. Switch to `--name-only` for reliable 159: matching. The `.../` prefix signals Git clipped the path to fit terminal width. 160: 161: --- 162: 163: ## 3. 9: # Mise Tool Management Skill
10: 
11: This skill defines the **layered industrial protocol** for managing `mise`-based development
12: environments. Each layer is a strict prerequisite for the one above it.
13: 
14: ```text
15: Layer 1: Mise Config Trust              (base — everything depends on this)
16: ├── Layer 2: Mise Tool Selection        (works on top of Layer 1)
17: │   └── Layer 3: Mise Python Setup      (a specialisation of Layer 2 for Python)
18: │       └── Layer 4: Mise Python Package Setup  (works on top of Layer 3)
19: ├── Layer 5: Bypass `mise exec` Cascade (alternative consumption path; sibling of Layer 2)
20: └── Layer 6: Deprecation Warning Handling & Backend Migration (cross-cuts Layers 1–5)
21: ```

23: ***
24: 
25: ## 1. Layer 1 — Mise Configuration Trust Protocol
26: 
27: `mise` blocks any config file it does not explicitly trust. The agent MUST resolve this
28: before attempting any tool use.
29: 
30: ### 1.1 Detection
31: 
32: Run the following command to detect whether any `mise` config in the working directory
33: is untrusted:
34: 
35: ```bash
36: # Attempt to list tools — mise prints trust errors to stderr
37: mise ls 2>&1
38: ```
39: 
40: - **Flag**: Output containing `Config files in ... are not trusted` signals an untrusted
41:   configuration.
42: 
43: ### 1.2 Analysis & Presentation
44: 
45: When a trust error is detected, the agent MUST:
46: 
47: 1. **Read** the untrusted `mise.toml` (or `.mise.toml`) file.
48: 2. **Present** the full file content to the USER in a fenced code block.
49: 3. **Analyse** each declared tool: what it is, what version is pinned, and why it exists.
50: 4. **Recommend** explicitly (e.g. "This file only pins `python = "3.11"`. It does not
51:    run scripts and poses no security risk. I recommend trusting it.").
52: 
53: ### 1.3 User Decision Gate
54: 
55: The agent MUST ask:
56: 
57: > "Do you want to trust this `mise.toml`? (yes / no)"
58: 
59: - **Yes** → run `mise trust` for the directory, then continue to Layer 2.
60: - **No** → halt. Document the decision. Do **not** attempt to use any `mise`-managed tool.
61: 
62: ### 1.4 Trust Command
63: 
64: ```bash
65: # Trust the config for the given directory
66: # Pass the config file path directly as the argument
67: mise trust /absolute/path/to/directory/mise.toml
68: ```
69: 
70: - The config file path is passed as a positional argument, not via `--path`.
71: - Note: mise prints trust-error noise during parsing even as it processes the command—
72:   this is expected. Confirm success by checking for `mise trusted <path>` in the output.
73: 
74: ***
75: 
76: ## 2. Layer 2 — Mise Tool Selection Protocol
77: 
78: Applies when a tool required by `mise.toml` is missing or could be satisfied by an
79: already-installed version. This layer applies to **any** `mise`-managed tool (Python,
80: Node, Go, etc.).
81: 
82: ### 2.1 Inventory
83: 
84: ```bash
85: # List every installed version of a tool (replace `python` with the tool name)
86: mise ls python --json
87: ```
88: 
89: Each JSON element has:
90: 
91: - `version` — installed version string
92: - `install_path` — filesystem path
93: - `source.path` — which `mise.toml` declared it
94: - `active` — whether it is the currently active version
95: 
96: ### 2.2 Required Version Freshness Check (Multi-Source)
97: 
98: Before comparison, check whether the version pinned in `mise.toml` is itself
99: the latest release of the tool. A single source is **not enough**: mise's
100: remote index can lag the upstream by hours-to-days, and a `github:<owner>/<repo>`
101: repackaging backend can lag the upstream language project by an entire minor
102: version. The agent MUST query up to three independent sources and present a
103: comparison table to the USER.
104: 
105: #### 2.2.1 Tier 1 — Mise Remote Index (always)
106: 
107: ```bash
108: # Newest versions known to mise's resolver:
109: mise ls-remote <tool>           | tail -5
110: mise ls-remote 'github:<owner>/<repo>' | tail -5
111: ```
112: 
113: #### 2.2.2 Tier 2 — Backend-Native Truth (for `github:` backend)
114: 
115: The GitHub Releases API publishes a release the moment the upstream maintainer
116: cuts it — before mise's index resync. Query it with the
117: [`github-repo-commit-fetch`](../github-repo-commit-fetch/SKILL.md) base
118: primitive `latest-release.py` (the shipped script, not an inline one-liner):
119: 
120: ```bash
121: python3 .agents/skills/github-repo-commit-fetch/scripts/latest-release.py \
122:     --repo <owner>/<repo>
123: # → {"tag_name": "0.69.0", "name": "0.69.0", "published_at": "..."}
124: ```
125: 
126: `--repo` is `owner/name` WITHOUT the `github:` prefix. Raw-curl fallback if
127: `gh` is unavailable (per `github-rest-api-fallback`):
128: 
129: ```bash
130: curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest \
131:     | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d["tag_name"], "-", d["name"])'
132: ```
133: 
134: For `ubi:`, `cargo:`, `npm:`, `pipx:`, and other backends, query the backend's
135: own registry (crates.io, npmjs.org, PyPI) for the same effect.
136: 
137: #### 2.2.3 Tier 3 — Upstream Language / Project Site (for repackaging backends)
138: 
139: When the backend is a community-maintained repackaging of an upstream language
140: or project (e.g., `github:adwinying/php` repackages PHP from php.net), the
141: upstream's own release feed is the meta-truth — it catches the case where the
142: repackager has not yet rebuilt the latest upstream release:
143: 
144: ```bash
145: # Example: official PHP latest from php.net
146: curl -s 'https://www.php.net/releases/index.php?json&max=1' \
147:     | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); k=list(d)[0]; print(k, "->", d[k]["version"])'
148: 
149: # Comparable feeds:
150: #   Python  → https://www.python.org/api/v2/downloads/release/?is_published=true
151: #   Node.js → https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json
152: #   Ruby    → https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/downloads/releases/ (HTML)
153: ```
154: 
155: If the repackager lags upstream by more than a patch release, surface that fact
156: in the presentation table — the user may want to wait, switch backends, or

164: Pinned in mise.toml         : github:adwinying/php 8.4.11
165: Tier 1 — mise ls-remote     : 8.5.6  (latest mise-known)
166: Tier 2 — GitHub Releases    : v8.5.6 (latest repackager release)
167: Tier 3 — php.net upstream   : 8.5.6  (latest upstream PHP)

181: - **If user wants latest** → install latest AND update `mise.toml` pin.

226: ### 2.5 User Decision Gate
227: 
228: 1. **Which version to use?** User selects from presented options.
229: 2. **Update `mise.toml` pin?** Only if user explicitly confirms.
230: 
231: ```bash
232: # Use an existing installed version — scoped to the config file, not globally
233: mise use --path /absolute/path/to/project python@<chosen-version>
234: 
235: # Install and use a new version — scoped to config
236: # Wrap mise install with scratch capture (see Layer 6) so deprecation warnings on
237: # stderr are preserved for audit:
238: #   SCRATCH="$(python3 <path>/repo-scratch-output-capture/scripts/ensure-scratch-gitignored.py)"
239: #   mise install python@<chosen-version> > "$SCRATCH/mise-install.out" 2> "$SCRATCH/mise-install.err"
240: mise install python@<chosen-version>
241: mise use --path /absolute/path/to/project python@<chosen-version>
242: ```
243: 
244: - `--path` — Ensures the `use` command writes to the **project-local** `mise.toml`,
245:   not the global `~/.config/mise/config.toml`. This prevents polluting the global env.
246: 
247: ### 2.6 Post-Bump Cleanup of Older Version (Same-Backend Bump)
248: 
249: When a user-approved bump installs `<tool>@<new>` while `<tool>@<old>` still
250: exists under the **same backend** (e.g., `github:adwinying/php` bumped from
251: `8.4.11` → `8.5.6`), the old install MUST be cleaned up so it does not consume
252: disk and does not confuse `mise ls`. The cleanup recipe for this case is
253: **sharply different** from the cross-backend migration cleanup in §6.5 — read
254: both before acting.
255: 
256: #### 2.6.1 Why §2.6 ≠ §6.5
257: 
258: | Axis | Same-backend bump (§2.6) | Cross-backend migration (§6.5) |
259: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
260: | Backend identity | Identical (`github:` → `github:`) | Changes (`ubi:` → `github:`) |
261: | Plugin install root | `~/.local/share/mise/installs/<backend>-<owner>-<repo>/` is **LIVE** (hosts the new install) | The old plugin root is **DEAD** (no version references it) |
262: | Alias symlinks (`<major>`, `<major>.<minor>`, `latest`) | Auto-repointed by mise to `<new>` on install — must be kept | Point at nothing valid — removed with plugin root |
263: | `mise uninstall <pkg>@<old>` | ✅ Sufficient | ✅ Necessary but **not** sufficient |
264: | `rm -rf <plugin-root>` | ❌ **FORBIDDEN** — destroys the live `<new>` install | ✅ Required follow-up to remove dangling alias symlinks |
265: 
266: #### 2.6.2 Procedure
267: 
268: Always with scratch capture per
269: [`repo-scratch-output-capture`](../repo-scratch-output-capture/SKILL.md):
270: 
271: ```bash
272: SCRATCH="$(python3 <path>/repo-scratch-output-capture/scripts/ensure-scratch-gitignored.py)"
273: 
274: # Step 1 — Uninstall the OLD version only (not the plugin root).
275: mise uninstall '<backend>:<owner>/<repo>@<old>' \
276:     > "$SCRATCH/mise-uninstall-<old>.out" 2> "$SCRATCH/mise-uninstall-<old>.err"
277: 
278: # Step 2 — Verify the plugin root remains LIVE with symlinks pointing at <new>.
279: ls -la "$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/<backend>-<owner>-<repo>/"
280: # Expected: <new>/ directory present; <major>, <major>.<minor>, latest -> ./<new>
281: 
282: # Step 3 — Verify only <new> is active.
283: mise current 2>&1 | grep -E '<tool>|<owner>'
284: mise ls '<backend>:<owner>/<repo>'
285: # Expected: a single row, version <new>.
286: 
287: # Step 4 — Optional smoke test of the binary.
288: mise exec -- <binary> --version
289: ```
290: 
291: If `ls -la` shows the symlinks STILL pointing at `<old>` (i.e., mise did not
292: re-link them on the new install — possible if the user never ran `mise install`
293: after editing the pin), re-run `mise install` from the project directory
294: **before** the `mise uninstall`. NEVER `rm -rf` the plugin root to "force" the
295: relink — that destroys `<new>`.
296: 
297: #### 2.6.3 Worked Example — `github:adwinying/php` 8.4.11 → 8.5.6
298: 
299: Real session against `Account-Ledger-Server-PHP/mise.toml` (2026-05-28):
300: 
301: ```bash
302: # Edit pin in mise.toml: "github:adwinying/php" = "8.5.6"
303: 
304: # Install new version with scratch capture.
305: SCRATCH="$(python3 .agents/skills/repo-scratch-output-capture/scripts/ensure-scratch-gitignored.py)"
306: mise install > "$SCRATCH/mise-install-8.5.6.out" 2> "$SCRATCH/mise-install-8.5.6.err"
307: # → Exit: 0 ; stderr shows download+verify+extract+✓ installed
308: 
309: mise current | grep php
310: # → github:adwinying/php 8.5.6
311: 
312: # Uninstall the old 8.4.11.
313: mise uninstall 'github:adwinying/php@8.4.11' \
314:     > "$SCRATCH/mise-uninstall-8.4.11.out" 2> "$SCRATCH/mise-uninstall-8.4.11.err"
315: # → mise github:adwinying/php@8.4.11   ✓ uninstalled
316: 
317: # Verify plugin root is LIVE, symlinks repointed.
318: ls -la ~/.local/share/mise/installs/github-adwinying-php/
319: # →  8     -> ./8.5.6
320: # →  8.5   -> ./8.5.6
321: # →  8.5.6/   (directory)
322: # →  latest -> ./8.5.6
323: # (no 8.4.11/ directory — cleaned)
324: 
325: mise ls 'github:adwinying/php'
326: # → 8.5.6  ~/lab-data/Account-Ledger-Server-PHP/mise.toml  8.5.6
327: ```

329: ### 2.7 Global-Scope Standalone Tool Install (No Project `mise.toml`)
330: 
331: Layers 2.1–2.6 assume a project-scoped `mise.toml` (`mise use --path`).
332: Some tools — standalone CLI utilities like `difftastic`, `bat`, `fzf` — are
333: user-level tools (usable across every project), not project-bound languages.
334: When the workspace has NO `mise.toml` (checked via `ls mise.toml .mise.toml`),
335: the Layer's decision path diverges: the pin goes into the **global**
336: `~/.config/mise/config.toml`, and the install targets the **full backend
337: specification string** rather than a bare tool name.
338: 
339: #### 2.7.1 Scope Decision Gate (ask the user)
340: 
341: | # | Scope | Command | When |
342: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
343: | ① | **Global config** (Recommended for standalone CLI tools) | pin in `~/.config/mise/config.toml` + `mise install '<backend>:<owner>/<repo>@<ver>'` | Tool is a user-level CLI meant to work in every project |
344: | ② | Project `mise.toml` | `mise use --path /abs/path/to/project <tool>@<ver>` | Tool is only needed in this repo, and a `mise.toml` exists or will be created |
345: | ③ | Install only, no pin | `mise install '<backend>:<owner>/<repo>@<ver>'` | One-off smoke test / evaluation; do not persist |
346: 
347: #### 2.7.2 Freshness + install (global path) — worked recipe
348: 
349: Version selection still runs the §2.2 multi-source freshness check (Tier 1
350: `mise ls-remote 'github:<owner>/<repo>'`, Tier 2 `latest-release.py`). Only the
351: config-target and the install string differ:
352: 
353: ```bash
354: # 1. Confirm NO project mise.toml anchors the tool.
355: ls mise.toml .mise.toml
356: 
357: # 2. Multi-source freshness (see §2.2):
358: mise ls-remote 'github:Wilfred/difftastic' | tail -5
359: python3 .agents/skills/github-repo-commit-fetch/scripts/latest-release.py --repo Wilfred/difftastic
360: 
361: # 3. Ask the user for scope (§2.7.1 ①/②/③). If ①:
362: #    Add to ~/.config/mise/config.toml under [tools]:
363: #      "github:Wilfred/difftastic" = "0.69.0"
364: 
365: # 4. Install the FULL backend spec with scratch capture (Layer 6).
366: SCRATCH="$(python3 .agents/skills/repo-scratch-output-capture/scripts/ensure-scratch-gitignored.py)"
367: mise install 'github:Wilfred/difftastic@0.69.0' \
368:     > "$SCRATCH/mise-install-difftastic.out" 2> "$SCRATCH/mise-install-difftastic.err"
369: 
370: # 5. Verify no deprecation warnings (Layer 6.1) and smoke-test the binary.
371: grep -E "deprecated|will be removed" "$SCRATCH/mise-install-difftastic.err" \
372:     || echo "no deprecation warnings"
373: mise exec -- difft --version
374: ```
375: 
376: Key differences from §2.5 (project path):
377: 
378: - **Pin location**: global `[tools]` in `~/.config/mise/config.toml`, added by
379:   direct config edit after explicit user approval — §2.5's project-scoped
380:   `--path` guarantee only applies when a project toml is the target.
381: - **Install string**: the FULL backend form `'<backend>:<owner>/<repo>@<version>'`
382:   (e.g. `'github:Wilfred/difftastic@0.69.0'`) — a bare `difftastic@0.69.0` does
383:   NOT resolve for a `github:` backend.
384: - **Binary name**: often differs from repo name (difftastic ships `difft`).
385:   Discover the shipped binary in
386:   `~/.local/share/mise/installs/github-Wilfred-difftastic/<ver>/` before the
387:   smoke test.
388: - **Scope gate is mandatory**: get user approval before BOTH the global-config
389:   edit AND the install — matching §10's prohibition on unprompted global
390:   mutation.

394: ## 3. Layer 3 — Mise Python Environment Setup
395: 
396: A specialisation of Layer 2 for the Python tool. Python requires extra steps to verify
397: the interpreter and `pip` are available through `mise exec`, preventing accidental use
398: of the system Python.
399: 
400: ### 3.1 Verify Python via `mise exec`
401: 
402: Always use `mise exec` to invoke Python, scoped to the correct configuration file:
403: 
404: ```bash
405: # Verify the exact Python version (not system Python)
406: mise exec --cd /absolute/path/to/project python@<version> -- python --version
407: 
408: # Verify pip is bundled with mise-managed Python
409: mise exec --cd /absolute/path/to/project python@<version> -- python -m pip --version
410: ```
411: 
412: - `mise exec` — Runs the command inside the mise environment, bypassing system PATH.
413: - `python@<version>` — Pins the exact version, preventing accidental tool resolution.
414: - `--cd /absolute/path/to/project` — Ensures the correct local `mise.toml` is loaded,
415:   NOT the global config.
416: - `--` — Separator between `mise exec` arguments and the actual command to run.
417: 
418: ### 3.2 Repair pip if Missing
419: 
420: ```bash
421: mise exec --cd /absolute/path/to/project python@<version> -- python -m ensurepip --upgrade
422: ```
423: 
424: Both verification commands MUST succeed before proceeding to Layer 4.
425: 
426: ### 3.3 Runtime Tool Resolution
427: 
428: When a script needs to invoke a mise-managed tool at runtime, use the
429: decision tree below.  Applies to any tool: Python, Node, Ruby, PHP, etc.
430: 
431: ```
432: Q: Does `<tool>` on PATH give an acceptable version?
433: ├── YES → Use `<tool>` directly (fastest, no cascade risk)
434: └── NO  → Q: Is there a mise.toml that pins this tool?
435:          ├── YES → Q: Does `mise exec` trigger unwanted cascade?
436:          │   ├── NO  → `mise exec --cd /project -- <tool> <args>`
437:          │   └── YES → Direct installation path:
438:          │              `~/.local/share/mise/installs/<tool>/<version>/bin/<tool>`
439:          └── NO  → Install via `mise install <tool>@<version>`
440: ```
441: 
442: **PATH resolution** — Works if the system or a mise shim puts a satisfactory
443: version on PATH.  Fastest approach, no risk of triggering cascade
444: installation of unrelated tools from `mise.toml`.
445: 
446: **`mise exec`** — Guarantees the correct tool version but can trigger
447: installation of *every* missing tool listed in `mise.toml` (the "cascade
448: risk").  Safe for single-tool configs; risky when `mise.toml` pins many
449: tools (e.g. Flutter + PHP + Java).
450: 
451: **Direct path** — Bypasses mise entirely by invoking the binary directly
452: from `~/.local/share/mise/installs/`.  Use when `mise exec` would trigger
453: cascade or when the mise environment is broken.  The version MUST be
454: pre-installed.
455: 
456: **`mise install`** — Last resort when no acceptable version exists anywhere.
457: Installs the specific version and makes it available for direct-path use.
458: 
459: Concrete examples:
460: 
461: ```bash
462: # Python — direct PATH (preferred)
463: python3 script.py
464: 
465: # Node — mise exec (single-tool config safe)
466: mise exec --cd /project -- node script.js
467: 
468: # Ruby — direct path (bypass cascade risk)
469: ~/.local/share/mise/installs/ruby/3.3.0/bin/ruby script.rb
470: 
471: # Install missing PHP
472: mise install php@8.3
473: ```
474: 
475: For the companion **documentation convention** (skill docs MUST use simplified
476: forms like `python3`, never fragile path commands in examples), see
477: [skill-factory mandate #7](../skill-factory/SKILL.md#2211-universal-script-mandates).
478:

481: ## 4. Layer 4 — Mise Python Package Setup Protocol
482: 
483: Applies when a Python package (e.g. `pylint`, `black`, `ruff`) is required but not
484: installed. Requires Layer 3 to be complete. Uses `jq` for JSON parsing — ensure
485: `jq` is installed via the [System-Wide Tool Management Skill](../system-wide-tool-management/SKILL.md)
486: before running §4.3.
487: 
488: ### 4.1 Requirements File Detection
489: 
490: Check whether a `requirements.txt` exists in the project scripts directory:
491: 
492: ```bash
493: # Use absolute path to avoid any working-directory ambiguity
494: ls /absolute/path/to/project/requirements.txt 2>/dev/null && echo "EXISTS" || echo "MISSING"
495: ```
496: 
497: ### 4.2 Package Entry Check
498: 
499: If `requirements.txt` exists, check whether the target package is listed:
500: 
501: ```bash
502: # Replace `pylint` with the package name; use absolute path
503: grep -i "^pylint" /absolute/path/to/project/requirements.txt
504: ```
505: 
506: ### 4.3 Version Freshness Check via PyPI (using `jq`)
507: 
508: If the package is listed, compare the pinned version against the latest on PyPI:
509: 
510: ```bash
511: # Get the latest published version from PyPI — requires jq (see system-wide-tool-management skill)
512: curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/pylint/json | jq -r '.info.version'
513: ```
514: 
515: - `curl -s` — Silent mode; suppresses progress output.
516: - `https://pypi.org/pypi/<package>/json` — PyPI JSON API endpoint for any package.
517: - `jq -r '.info.version'` — Extracts the `version` field from `info` as raw text.
518:   The `-r` flag removes surrounding quotes.
519: 
520: ### 4.4 Decision Table
521: 
522: | State | Action |
523: | :--- | :--- |
524: | `requirements.txt` missing | Create it; add `<package>==<latest>` |
525: | Package not in `requirements.txt` | Add `<package>==<latest>` |
526: | Package pinned to outdated version | Present analysis; offer to update pin to latest |
527: | Package pinned to latest | Proceed directly to installation |
528: 
529: If pinned version is **not** the latest:
530: 
531: 1. Present comparison to user (pinned vs latest).
532: 2. Ask: "Update pin to latest and install?"
533: 3. **User says yes to latest** → update pin, install.
534: 4. **User says no to latest** → install the pinned version as-is. Do NOT alter
535:    `requirements.txt`.
536: 
537: ### 4.5 Presentation to User
538: 
539: The agent MUST present its analysis, for example:
540: 
541: ```text
542: requirements.txt  : /absolute/path/to/project/requirements.txt — EXISTS
543: pylint entry      : MISSING
544: Latest on PyPI    : 3.3.4
545: 
546: Recommendation:
547:   Add `pylint==3.3.4` to requirements.txt, then install via:
548:   mise exec python@3.11.9 -- python -m pip install -r /absolute/path/to/project/requirements.txt
549: ```
550: 
551: ### 4.6 User Decision Gate
552: 
553: > "Approve adding `pylint==<version>` to `requirements.txt` and installing? (yes / no)"
554: 
555: ### 4.7 Installation
556: 
557: Upon approval, always use `mise exec` with an absolute path to `requirements.txt`:
558: 
559: ```bash
560: # Install all packages declared in requirements.txt into the active mise python env
561: mise exec --cd /absolute/path/to/project python@<version> -- \
562:   python -m pip install -r /absolute/path/to/project/requirements.txt
563: ```
564: 
565: - `mise exec --cd ... python@<version>` — Targets the exact mise-managed Python,
566:   not the system interpreter. This ensures packages land in the correct isolated environment.
567: - `python -m pip` — Uses the pip bundled with the `mise`-managed Python.
568: - `-r /absolute/path/to/project/requirements.txt` — Reads the pinned dependency file for reproducible installs.
569:   Absolute path eliminates any working-directory ambiguity.
570: 
571: ### 4.8 Execution Verification
572: 
573: After installation, verify the tool works:
574: 
575: ```bash
576: # Example: verify pylint is reachable and show its version
577: mise exec --cd /absolute/path/to/project python@<version> -- python -m pylint --version
578: ```

582: ## 5. Layer 5 — Bypass `mise exec` Cascade Protocol
583: 
584: `mise exec` walks UP the directory tree from the current working directory and, for every
585: trusted `mise.toml` it finds, ensures **every pinned tool** is installed before running your
586: command. From an unrelated repo, a one-shot `mise exec -- python script.py` can trigger
587: multi-GB downloads of Flutter, PHP, Composer, etc. — completely unrelated to the actual task.
588: 
589: This layer documents the **direct-binary invocation** alternative: invoke the mise-installed
590: binary by its concrete install path, which is still mise-managed (versioned, isolated from
591: system Python), but skips the trust-chain walk that triggers the cascade.
592: 
593: ### 5.1 Detection — Are You at Risk of a Cascade?
594: 
595: Run from the CWD where you'd otherwise call `mise exec`:
596: 
597: ```bash
598: mise current 2>&1
599: ```
600: 
601: If the output lists tools you do NOT need for the current task (e.g., `flutter@3.22.3`,
602: `php@8.4.11`, `composer@...`, `ubi:adwinying/php`), `mise exec` will attempt to install all of
603: them before running your command. Cascade risk = HIGH.
604: 
605: ### 5.2 Resolution — Direct-Binary Path
606: 
607: The mise install root is conventionally:
608: 
609: ```text
610: $HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/<tool>/<version>/bin/<binary>
611: ```
612: 
613: To find the version directory for a given tool:
614: 
615: ```bash
616: ls "$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/<tool>" | sort -V | tail -1
617: ```
618: 
619: Then invoke directly — no shim, no trust walk, no cascade:
620: 
621: ```bash
622: python3 --version
623: python3 -m pip install --user pymysql
624: ```
625: 
626: **This is NOT the same as invoking from `$PATH`.** The prohibition in §10 against "Invoking
627: `python` or `pip` from PATH" targets unmanaged system binaries (`/usr/bin/python3` on macOS
628: is Apple Xcode 3.9, not your pinned version). The Layer 5 path is an explicit, version-pinned
629: mise install — fully consistent with the environment-management mandate.
630: 
631: ### 5.3 When to Prefer Layer 5 over Layers 3/4
632: 
633: | Situation | Use Layer 3/4 (`mise exec`) | Use Layer 5 (direct path) |
634: | --- | --- | --- |
635: | CWD is the project that pins the tool | ✅ | — |
636: | CWD has NO `mise.toml` in ancestry | ✅ | acceptable |
637: | CWD's ancestor `mise.toml` pins UNRELATED tools (cascade risk) | ❌ | ✅ |
638: | Running a one-shot probe from an unrelated repo | ❌ | ✅ |
639: | CI / scripted invocation where install side-effects are forbidden | ❌ | ✅ |
640: 
641: ### 5.4 Stream Convention Note (`mise trust` and Friends)
642: 
643: `mise trust`, `mise install`, and similar housekeeping commands write their confirmation
644: messages to **stderr**, not stdout, per Unix convention (stdout reserved for pipeable data
645: such as resolved paths; stderr for diagnostics). If you redirect only stdout to a log file
646: you will see an empty log and misinterpret the command as silently failing — always pair
647: `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log` or use `2>&1` when capturing.
648: 
649: This convention is shared with `git`, `cargo`, `rustup`, `npm` (for non-data output), and
650: most modern CLIs.
651: 
652: ### 5.5 Cleanup After an Accidentally-Triggered Cascade
653: 
654: If `mise exec` was invoked from an unsafe CWD and partial installs leaked, clean up:
655: 
656: ```bash
657: # 1. List recent mise installs (lots of dirs = cascade evidence).
658: ls -lt "$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/" | head
659: 
660: # 2. Remove specific unwanted tool installs.
661: rm -rf "$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/flutter/<version>"
662: rm -rf "$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/ubi-adwinying-php"
663: rm -rf "$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/ubi-composer-composer"
664: rm -rf "$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/vfox-version-fox-vfox-php-<version>"
665: 
666: # 3. Remove partial download archives.
667: rm -f "$HOME/.cache/mise/<tool>/<version>.zip"
668: ```
669: 
670: Verify nothing the user actually wanted got deleted:
671: 
672: ```bash
673: mise ls
674: ```
675: 
676: ### 5.6 Consumers of Layer 5
677: 
678: - [`mysql-capability-probe-pymysql`](../mysql-capability-probe-pymysql/SKILL.md) — its
679:   `probe-runner.py` resolves python via Layer 5 to avoid the cascade when probing from any
680:   repo other than the python's home project.
681: - PHP `php -l` syntax linting outside the PHP-pinned project — resolve the binary directly
682:   at `~/.local/share/mise/installs/github-adwinying-php/<version>/php`. NOTE: the

686:   before scripting an invocation.

691: ## 6. Layer 6 — Deprecation Warning Handling & Backend Migration Protocol
692: 
693: `mise` emits deprecation warnings on **stderr** (e.g.
694: `mise WARN  deprecated [ubi]: The ubi backend is deprecated. Use the github
695: backend instead …`) the first time an affected tool is resolved. Because the
696: warning is on stderr and `mise install` is otherwise terse on success, the
697: warning is **invisible** unless stderr is captured. This layer mandates the
698: capture, surfaces the warning to the user, and drives the `mise.toml` migration.
699: 
700: ### 6.1 Capture-First Detection
701: 
702: Every `mise install` / `mise trust` / `mise ls` invocation in an unattended or
703: agent-driven flow MUST be wrapped in the scratch-capture pattern from the
704: [`repo-scratch-output-capture`](../repo-scratch-output-capture/SKILL.md) base
705: skill. The scratch skill is the SSOT for the capture mechanics — this skill
706: only specifies *what* to capture and *how to react* to the captured content.
707: 
708: ```bash
709: SCRATCH="$(python3 <path-to>/repo-scratch-output-capture/scripts/ensure-scratch-gitignored.py)"
710: mise install \
711:     > "$SCRATCH/mise-install.out" \
712:     2> "$SCRATCH/mise-install.err"
713: echo "Exit: $?"
714: ```
715: 
716: After every invocation, grep stderr for deprecation signals:
717: 
718: ```bash
719: grep -E "deprecated|will be removed" "$SCRATCH/mise-install.err" || \
720:     echo "(no deprecation warnings)"
721: ```
722: 
723: ### 6.2 Known Backend Deprecations
724: 
725: | Deprecated form in `mise.toml` | Replacement | Removal version | Notes |
726: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
727: | `"ubi:<owner>/<repo>" = "<ver>"` | `"github:<owner>/<repo>" = "<ver>"` | mise `2027.1.0` | The `ubi` backend is deprecated workspace-wide; the `github` backend is the direct successor and supports the same `<owner>/<repo>` slug. |
728: 
729: This table is the project's living deprecation registry. When `mise` introduces
730: a new deprecation, add a row here in the same change that documents the
731: migration — do NOT scatter migration notes across consumer projects.
732: 
733: ### 6.3 Migration Decision Gate
734: 
735: When stderr contains a deprecation warning, the agent MUST:
736: 
737: 1. **Present** the literal warning text to the user (quoted from the captured
738:    `.err` file).
739: 2. **Identify** the affected entry in `mise.toml` (file path + line number +
740:    current value).
741: 3. **Propose** the literal replacement form from §6.2.
742: 4. **Cite** the removal version (so the user can decide urgency vs. risk).
743: 5. **Ask**: "Migrate `<old>` → `<new>` in `mise.toml`? (yes / no)"
744: 
745: The `mise.toml` MUST NOT be edited without explicit user approval, in keeping
746: with the general prohibition in §10.
747: 
748: ### 6.4 Migration Execution
749: 
750: Upon approval, perform the edit, re-install with scratch capture, and verify
751: no deprecation warning remains:
752: 
753: ```bash
754: # 1. Edit mise.toml (literal replacement; preserve quoting and indentation).
755: #    Use whatever in-place editor is appropriate; verify with diff.
756: #    Example transformation:
757: #      "ubi:adwinying/php"    = "8.4.11"
758: #    →  "github:adwinying/php" = "8.4.11"
759: 
760: # 2. Re-run install with scratch capture.
761: SCRATCH="$(python3 <path-to>/repo-scratch-output-capture/scripts/ensure-scratch-gitignored.py)"
762: mise install \
763:     > "$SCRATCH/mise-install-postmigration.out" \
764:     2> "$SCRATCH/mise-install-postmigration.err"
765: 
766: # 3. Verify warning is gone.
767: grep -E "deprecated|will be removed" "$SCRATCH/mise-install-postmigration.err" \
768:     && echo "STILL DEPRECATED — investigate" \
769:     || echo "Migration verified clean."
770: 
771: # 4. (Optional) Validate the edited mise.toml per §9.2.
772: taplo check /absolute/path/to/project/mise.toml
773: taplo fmt --check /absolute/path/to/project/mise.toml
774: ```
775: 
776: ### 6.5 Stale-Install Cleanup
777: 
778: > **Contrast pointer**: §6.5 applies ONLY when the backend identifier itself
779: > changed (e.g., `ubi:` → `github:`), so the OLD plugin root is dead. For a
780: > same-backend version bump (e.g., `github:` 8.4.11 → 8.5.6) the plugin root
781: > is still LIVE and `rm -rf` of it would destroy the new install — use §2.6
782: > instead.
783: 
784: After a successful backend migration, the previous backend's install directory
785: under `~/.local/share/mise/installs/` is no longer referenced by `mise.toml`
786: but still consumes disk. The cleanup is **two-step** because `mise uninstall`
787: only removes the version directory — it does NOT remove the version-aliasing
788: symlinks (`8`, `8.4`, `latest`) that pointed to it, leaving them dangling.
789: 
790: Step 1 — Uninstall via mise (preferred over raw `rm -rf` so mise's internal
791: registry, caches, and `.mise.backend.toml` are all cleaned up):
792: 
793: ```bash
794: SCRATCH="$(python3 <path>/repo-scratch-output-capture/scripts/ensure-scratch-gitignored.py)"
795: mise uninstall 'ubi:<owner>/<repo>@<version>' \
796:     > "$SCRATCH/mise-uninstall.out" 2> "$SCRATCH/mise-uninstall.err"
797: ```
798: 
799: Step 2 — Remove the now-empty plugin root and its dangling symlinks:
800: 
801: ```bash
802: ls -la "$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/ubi-<owner>-<repo>/"   # confirm only dangling symlinks remain
803: rm -rf "$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/ubi-<owner>-<repo>"
804: ```
805: 
806: Step 3 — Verify the deprecated entry is gone and the replacement is active:
807: 
808: ```bash
809: mise current 2>&1 | grep -E '<tool>|<owner>'
810: # → github:<owner>/<repo> <version>   (no ubi: line)
811: ```
812: 
813: For wholesale removal after an accidentally-triggered cascade (multiple
814: unrelated tools to delete), §5.5 owns the bulk `rm -rf` recipe; this section
815: owns the targeted single-tool migration cleanup.
816:

856: ## 7. Layer 7 — Plugin Installation & Backend Selection Protocol
857: 
858: Mise plugins frequently exist under multiple competing backends
859: (`asdf:`, `vfox:`, `github:`, `aqua:`, `ubi:`). The choice is **not
860: interchangeable** — different backends ship different binaries, manage
861: their own install roots, and have different SSH / HTTPS reachability
862: profiles on different networks. This Layer runs **before** Layers 1–6:
863: no version pin, no trust prompt, no `mise install` invocation can
864: succeed if the underlying plugin is missing or installed under a
865: backend that doesn't resolve in the current environment.
866: 
867: ### 7.1 Detection
868: 
869: Apply this Layer whenever:
870: 
871: - The user issues `mise install <plugin>` (single-plugin install)
872: - The user issues `mise install` in a project folder and it fails with
873:   a plugin-resolution error (e.g., `plugin <name> not found`, SSH
874:   authentication failure resolving an `asdf:` or `vfox:` URL, or
875:   `mise registry` returning multiple candidates)
876: - A `mise.toml` references a tool whose plugin is not yet installed
877:   locally (`mise plugins --user` does not list it)
878: 
879: ### 7.2 Backend Inventory
880: 
881: Query the mise registry for all available backends for the plugin:
882: 
883: ```bash
884: # Show every registered backend for a given tool name
885: mise registry <plugin>
886: ```
887: 
888: If the output lists more than one entry (e.g., `dart` may show
889: `asdf:asdf-community/asdf-dart` and `vfox:version-fox/vfox-dart`), the
890: plugin has **multiple backends** and the user MUST choose explicitly —
891: never auto-pick the first match.
892: 
893: ### 7.3 Presentation to User
894: 
895: Present a numbered table of every backend candidate with its full
896: GitHub URL and a brief differentiator:
897: 
898: | # | Backend | Repo | Notes |
899: |---|---|---|---|
900: | 1 | `asdf:` | `asdf-community/asdf-dart` | Mature, large user base |
901: | 2 | `vfox:` | `version-fox/vfox-dart`    | Newer, cross-platform Lua plugin runtime |
902: 
903: Ask the user which to install. Do NOT proceed without an explicit
904: choice.
905: 
906: ### 7.4 Installation — Full GitHub URL Form
907: 
908: Once the user has chosen a backend, install the plugin using the
909: **full HTTPS GitHub URL** of the chosen backend's repository:
910: 
911: ```bash
912: mise plugins install <plugin> https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git
913: ```
914: 
915: **Forbidden form — `vfox:` / `asdf:` URL prefixes:**
916: 
917: ```bash
918: # ❌ DO NOT USE — these prefixes cause SSH auth failures on networks
919: #    that lack a configured GitHub SSH key, even when the user is
920: #    fully authenticated for HTTPS clones.
921: mise plugins install <plugin> vfox:version-fox/vfox-<plugin>
922: mise plugins install <plugin> asdf:asdf-community/asdf-<plugin>
923: ```
924: 
925: The HTTPS `.git` URL form sidesteps the SSH-key requirement and works
926: identically on Gitpod, Cloud Shell, NeverInstall, plain Ubuntu, macOS,
927: and Windows.
928: 
929: ### 7.5 Triggering the Tool Install
930: 
931: **`mise.toml` precedence — Layer 7 never overrides it.** Layer 7
932: activates only when (a) the user issues a bare-plugin
933: `mise install <plugin>` outside of `mise.toml` control, or (b) a
934: project-folder `mise install` has already failed with a plugin-
935: resolution error. While `mise.toml` resolves cleanly, Layer 7 is a
936: no-op; the agent MUST NOT pre-emptively prompt for a backend choice
937: on plugins that `mise.toml` is silently happy with.
938: 
939: After the plugin lands, invoke the actual tool install. Two cases:
940: 
941: **Single-plugin install (user originally said `mise install <plugin>`):**
942: 
943: ```bash
944: mise install <plugin>
945: ```
946: 
947: This installs the latest version known to the freshly-installed
948: plugin's backend. From here, hand off to **Layer 2** (§2) for
949: version-freshness review and pinning.
950: 
951: **Project-folder install (user originally said `mise install`):**
952: 
953: ```bash
954: mise install
955: ```
956: 
957: This re-reads `mise.toml` and installs every pinned tool. If a
958: previous `mise install` attempt failed because the wrong-backend
959: plugin was installed, first **uninstall** the problematic backend
960: plugin before re-trying:
961: 
962: ```bash
963: mise plugins uninstall <plugin>
964: mise plugins install <plugin> https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git
965: mise install
966: ```
967: 
968: ### 7.6 Verification
969: 
970: After any plugin install, verify the registered backend URL:
971: 
972: ```bash
973: mise plugins --urls --user
974: ```
975: 
976: The output MUST show the plugin name mapped to the exact HTTPS URL
977: chosen in §7.3. If a `vfox:` or `asdf:` prefix appears instead, the
978: install bypassed this Layer — uninstall and re-run with the HTTPS
979: form before proceeding.
980: 
981: ### 7.7 Decision Matrix (Quick Reference)
982: 
983: | User says | mise registry returns | Action |
984: |---|---|---|
985: | `mise install <plugin>` | 1 backend | Install with HTTPS URL (§7.4), then `mise install <plugin>` (§7.5) |
986: | `mise install <plugin>` | ≥ 2 backends | Present table (§7.3), get user choice, then §7.4 + §7.5 |
987: | `mise install` in project | succeeds | No-op — Layer 7 does not apply |
988: | `mise install` in project | fails with plugin error | Identify failed plugin, check `mise registry <plugin>` for alternatives, if ≥ 2: present table (§7.3) → uninstall (§7.5 second case) → reinstall via HTTPS → retry |
989: 
990: ### 7.8 Worked Examples
991: 
992: #### 7.8.1 Scenario A — Bare-plugin install, multi-backend choice
993: 
994: User says: `mise install dart`
995: 
996: ```bash
997: $ mise registry dart
998: asdf:asdf-community/asdf-dart
999: vfox:version-fox/vfox-dart
1000: ```
1001: 
1002: Two backends → Layer 7 applies. Agent prompts (literal phrasing from
1003: the source rule):
1004: 
1005: > *"dart has asdf and vfox backends, which do you prefer?"*
1006: 
1007: User picks `asdf:`. Agent runs:
1008: 
1009: ```bash
1010: mise plugins install dart https://github.com/asdf-community/asdf-dart.git
1011: mise install dart
1012: mise plugins --urls --user | grep dart
1013: # dart  https://github.com/asdf-community/asdf-dart.git
1014: ```
1015: 
1016: Layer 7 complete. Hand off to Layer 2 for version pin.
1017: 
1018: #### 7.8.2 Scenario B — Project-folder install fails, fallback to alternate backend
1019: 
1020: User runs `mise install` in a project folder pinning `dart`. The
1021: currently-installed plugin backend (e.g., `asdf:asdf-community/asdf-dart`)
1022: fails to resolve — network rejects the upstream tarball, the asdf
1023: shim crashes, or the binary fails to launch post-install. Agent
1024: checks `mise registry dart`, sees `vfox:` is also available, and
1025: prompts (literal phrasing from the source rule):
1026: 
1027: > *"dart installation failed, try vfox backend instead?"*
1028: 
1029: User confirms. Agent runs:
1030: 
1031: ```bash
1032: mise plugins uninstall dart
1033: mise plugins install dart https://github.com/version-fox/vfox-dart.git
1034: mise install
1035: mise plugins --urls --user | grep dart
1036: # dart  https://github.com/version-fox/vfox-dart.git
1037: ```
1038: 
1039: `mise.toml` is unchanged (Layer 7 swaps the backend, never the
1040: version pin). Hand off to Layer 2 only if the user now wants to bump
1041: the version.

1132: ## 9. Post-Edit File Validation Protocol
1133: 
1134: After **any** edit to a project file, the agent MUST validate the file using its
1135: industrial-standard tool before proceeding. This catches formatting errors (e.g. stray
1136: indentation) introduced by automated edits.
1137: 
1138: > The validation tools listed here are **system-wide tools**. Ensure they are installed
1139: > using the [System-Wide Tool Management Skill](../system-wide-tool-management/SKILL.md)
1140: > before running these commands.
1141: 
1142: ### 9.1 Validation Commands by File Type
1143: 
1144: | File | Tool | Syntax Check | Format Check & Fix |
1145: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
1146: | `mise.toml` | `taplo` | `taplo check <absolute_path>` | `taplo fmt --check <absolute_path>` / `taplo fmt <absolute_path>` |
1147: | `requirements.txt` | `pip` | `pip install --dry-run -r <absolute_path>` | N/A (no formatter) |
1148: | `*.md` Markdown | `markdownlint-cli2` | `markdownlint-cli2 <absolute_path>` | `markdownlint-cli2 --fix <absolute_path>` |
1149: | `*.py` Python | `pylint` via `mise exec` | `mise exec --cd <project_dir> python@<ver> -- python -m pylint <absolute_path>` | Manual fix per error |
1150: 
1151: > **Note on Python Errors & Formatting:**
1152: >
1153: > - `pylint` is a strict, comprehensive linter. It highlights semantic and structural
1154: >   errors (e.g., missing docstrings, generic exceptions, complexity limits) which
1155: >   **must be fixed manually** via code edits.
1156: > - **DO NOT manually fix Pylint errors** before exhausting auto-fixers. You MUST use
1157: >   specialized formatters and auto-fixers first to resolve stylistic and structural
1158: >   complaints automatically.
1159: > - **Primary Industrial Standard**: Use **`ruff check --fix`** and **`ruff format`** first.
1160: >   It is drastically faster and can auto-fix many structural and code-style issues.
1161: > - **Secondary Standard (Fallback)**: If `ruff` cannot be used, youMUST use **`black`**.
1162: >   `black` is the definitive, uncompromising Python code formatter and was the
1163: >   industry standard before `ruff`. (Only use `autopep8` as a last-resort legacy fallback).
1164: > - Only after running these auto-fixers should you manually fix any remaining semantic
1165: >   Pylint errors (e.g., missing docstrings, complex logic).
1166: > - Because these are Python tools, they MUST follow Layer 4: add them to
1167: >   `requirements.txt` and run them via `mise exec`.
1168: 
1169: ### 9.2 `mise.toml` Validation & Formatting (`taplo`)
1170: 
1171: > **Important distinction:**
1172: >
1173: > - `taplo check` — validates TOML **syntax** (parse errors, duplicate keys). A file can
1174: >   pass `check` but still be incorrectly formatted.
1175: > - `taplo fmt --check` — verifies **formatting** (indentation, spacing, alignment).
1176: > - `taplo fmt` — **auto-fixes** formatting in place; run after `check` passes.
1177: 
1178: Always run **both** steps in order:
1179: 
1180: ```bash
1181: # taplo must be installed — use system-wide-tool-management skill if missing
1182: # Step 1 — Syntax check (exits 1 if invalid TOML)
1183: taplo check /absolute/path/to/project/mise.toml
1184: 
1185: # Step 2 — Formatting check (exits 1 if not properly formatted)
1186: taplo fmt --check /absolute/path/to/project/mise.toml
1187: 
1188: # Step 3 — Auto-format if Step 2 fails (modifies file in place)
1189: taplo fmt /absolute/path/to/project/mise.toml
1190: 
1191: # Step 4 — Re-run formatting check to confirm clean
1192: taplo fmt --check /absolute/path/to/project/mise.toml
1193: ```
1194: 
1195: - ✅ `taplo check`: exit 0, output `found files total=1` with no ERROR lines
1196: - ✅ `taplo fmt --check`: exit 0 (no output on success)
1197: - ❌ `taplo fmt --check` exit 1: `ERROR ... the file is not properly formatted` — run
1198:   `taplo fmt` to auto-fix
1199: 
1200: Common TOML formatting mistakes:
1201: 
1202: - Leading indentation on key-value pairs under a table header.
1203:     - ❌ Incorrect: `python = "3.11"` (4 spaces before `python`)
1204:     - ✅ Correct: `python = "3.11"` (Starts securely at the beginning of the line)
1205: - Missing blank line separating table sections
1206: - Inconsistent quote style
1207: 
1208: ### 9.3 `requirements.txt` Validation (`pip`)
1209: 
1210: ```bash
1211: pip install --dry-run -r /absolute/path/to/project/requirements.txt 2>&1 \
1212:   | grep -E "^(Collecting|Requirement already|ERROR|WARNING)"
1213: ```
1214: 
1215: - ✅ Success: only `Collecting` and `Requirement already satisfied` lines; exit 0
1216: - ❌ Failure: any `ERROR` line — fix the package specifier before proceeding
1217: - No auto-formatter for `requirements.txt`; fix manually.

1248: 
1249: The agent is FORBIDDEN from:

Move it OUT of the working tree (e.g., to 890: `/../scratch/` or a personal-sandbox branch). 891: - **Disposable** — content already represented in the index, HEAD, 892: or another branch. Delete directly. 893: 894: 3. **Verify** before committing: re-run the §3h detect command and 895: confirm zero matches. Sidecars MUST NOT be added to `.gitignore` 896: as a substitute for cleanup — that hides the symptom and lets the 897: next session re-encounter the same disposal decision blind. 898: 899: 4. **NEVER `git add` a sidecar** "to clean up history later". Runs `git diff [--cached] -- ` to capture the full patch. 956: 2. Parses the unified diff into a header (before the first `@@`) and a 957: list of hunks (each `@@ ... @@` block with its context and changes). 958: 3. For each hunk, checks whether ANY of the `--match` substrings or 959: `--match-regex` patterns appear anywhere in the hunk text (context 960: lines, old lines, AND new lines). 961: 4. Reconstructs a filtered patch from the header + matching hunks only. 962: 5. Runs `git apply --cached` with the filtered patch to stage exactly 963: those hunks into the index. Non-matching hunks remain unstaged. 964: 965: **Complementary primitives (delegated to base skill `git-hunk-staging-primitives`):** 966: 967: | Script | Action | Used in | 968: |---|---|---| 969: | `stage-hunk-from-diff.py` | Stage ONLY matching hunks | §3i (this section) | 970: | `stage-file-excluding-lines.py` | Stage file MINUS matching lines | §2f.1 | 971: | `agents-md-stage-row.py` | Stage exactly one AGENTS.md row | §2f | 972: | `stage-head-synthesize.py` | Stage HEAD with substitutions | §13 | 973: | `stage-specific-hunks.py` | Stage specific hunk indices | §3i.1, §13 | 974: | `git add -p` | Interactive hunk-by-hunk staging | §3a–§3f | 975: 976: **Edge cases:** 977: 978: - **Zero hunks matched:** exits with error. Use `--check` to preview. 979: - **File has no diff:** exits with error (nothing to extract). 980: - **Filtered patch wouldn't apply:** `--check` reveals the issue. 981: Common causes: the index has drifted from HEAD (e.g., some changes 982: already staged for this file). Use `--cached` to target staged 983: changes, or commit/reset the existing staged content first. 984: 985: **See also:** `stage-hunk-from-diff.py --help` for full argument docs. 986: 987: #### 3i.1 — Adjacent-Lines Isolation (git add -p Split Failure Fallback) 988: 989: When `git add -p` presents a single hunk with multiple adjacent 990: added or deleted lines and `s` (split) returns "Sorry, cannot split 991: this hunk," the lines are too close (no intervening context line) for 992: Git's hunk-split algorithm. `stage-hunk-from-diff.py` (§3i) stages 993: the ENTIRE hunk when ANY line matches your filter — it cannot isolate 994: individual adjacent lines within a hunk. 995: 996: **Preferred fallback:** `stage-file-excluding-lines.py` (§2f.1) stages 997: the file with the unwanted line(s) EXCLUDED, leaving the working tree 998: untouched. Updates the index entry via `git update-index --cacheinfo`. 1023: 5. Working tree is never modified — the excluded line persists on disk. 1024: 1025: **Why prefer this over manual editing (Intermediate State Synthesis, 1026: §13):** 1027: 1028: - Zero working-tree mutation — no risk of forgetting the restore step. 1029: - The index blob is computed from the exact working-tree content 1030: (minus matched lines) — no accidental whitespace drift from a 1031: manual copy. 1032: - Audit trail: the script logs the excluded line content + blob SHA 1033: to stderr. 1034: 1035: **When manual editing is still appropriate (fallback to §13):** 1036: 1037: - The script is unavailable (no `.agents/` tree, or Python not on PATH). 1038: - Lines to exclude span multiple non-adjacent positions (one 1039: `--exclude` call handles one line; for scattered exclusions, manual 1040: may be faster). 1041: 1042: --- 1043: 1044: ### Step 4 — Formatting & Structural Partitioning 1045: 1046: Stylistic and structural changes MUST be explicitly separated from 1047: functional commits. 1048: 1049: #### 4a — Formatting & Stylistic Consolidation 1050: 1051: **Target:** Purely aesthetic changes — indentation, whitespace, 1052: Markdown header-level corrections, single blank line adjustments. 1053: 1054: **Rule:** If multiple files require these adjustments, club them into a 1055: single dedicated commit.
